1086: .. function:: fsync(fd)
1087: 
1088:    Force write of file with filedescriptor *fd* to disk.  On Unix, this calls the
1089:    native :c:func:`!fsync` function; on Windows, the MS :c:func:`!_commit` function.
1090: 
1091:    If you're starting with a buffered Python :term:`file object` *f*, first do
1092:    ``f.flush()``, and then do ``os.fsync(f.fileno())``, to ensure that all internal
1093:    buffers associated with *f* are written to disk.
1094: 
1095:    .. availability:: Unix, Windows.

2676: .. function:: rename(src, dst, *, src_dir_fd=None, dst_dir_fd=None)
2677: 
2678:    Rename the file or directory *src* to *dst*. If *dst* exists, the operation
2679:    will fail with an :exc:`OSError` subclass in a number of cases:
2680: 
2681:    On Windows, if *dst* exists a :exc:`FileExistsError` is always raised.
2682:    The operation may fail if *src* and *dst* are on different filesystems. Use
2683:    :func:`shutil.move` to support moves to a different filesystem.
2684: 
2685:    On Unix, if *src* is a file and *dst* is a directory or vice-versa, an
2686:    :exc:`IsADirectoryError` or a :exc:`NotADirectoryError` will be raised
2687:    respectively.  If both are directories and *dst* is empty, *dst* will be
2688:    silently replaced.  If *dst* is a non-empty directory, an :exc:`OSError`
2689:    is raised. If both are files, *dst* will be replaced silently if the user
2690:    has permission.  The operation may fail on some Unix flavors if *src* and
2691:    *dst* are on different filesystems.  If successful, the renaming will be an
2692:    atomic operation (this is a POSIX requirement).
2693: 
2694:    This function can support specifying *src_dir_fd* and/or *dst_dir_fd* to
2695:    supply :ref:`paths relative to directory descriptors <dir_fd>`.
2696: 
2697:    If you want cross-platform overwriting of the destination, use :func:`replace`.
2698: 
2699:    .. audit-event:: os.rename src,dst,src_dir_fd,dst_dir_fd os.rename
2700:

2708: .. function:: renames(old, new)
2709: 
2710:    Recursive directory or file renaming function. Works like :func:`rename`, except
2711:    creation of any intermediate directories needed to make the new pathname good is
2712:    attempted first. After the rename, directories corresponding to rightmost path
2713:    segments of the old name will be pruned away using :func:`removedirs`.
2714: 
2715:    .. note::
2716: 
2717:       This function can fail with the new directory structure made if you lack
2718:       permissions needed to remove the leaf directory or file.
2719: 
2720:    .. audit-event:: os.rename src,dst,src_dir_fd,dst_dir_fd os.renames
2721: 
2722:    .. versionchanged:: 3.6
2723:       Accepts a :term:`path-like object` for *old* and *new*.

2726: .. function:: replace(src, dst, *, src_dir_fd=None, dst_dir_fd=None)
2727: 
2728:    Rename the file or directory *src* to *dst*.  If *dst* is a non-empty directory,
2729:    :exc:`OSError` will be raised.  If *dst* exists and is a file, it will
2730:    be replaced silently if the user has permission.  The operation may fail
2731:    if *src* and *dst* are on different filesystems.  If successful,
2732:    the renaming will be an atomic operation (this is a POSIX requirement).
2733: 
2734:    This function can support specifying *src_dir_fd* and/or *dst_dir_fd* to
2735:    supply :ref:`paths relative to directory descriptors <dir_fd>`.
2736: 
2737:    .. audit-event:: os.rename src,dst,src_dir_fd,dst_dir_fd os.replace
